ev.q: The child and adolescent immunization schedule is published annually to consolidate and summarize updates to ACIP recommendations

public_health_question.v: What changes did ACIP make in the 2023 recommended immunization schedule for children and adolescents aged 18 years or younger?

ev.q: summarizes ACIP recommendations, including several changes from the 2022 immunization schedule
A new section was added to provide additional details on the use of COVID-19 vaccines.
The note has been updated to reflect the recommendations for the 2022–23 influenza season.
PCV15 can be used interchangeably in both healthy children and those with any risk for invasive pneumococcal disease
updated to include recommendations for additional MMR doses in a mumps outbreak setting.
clarify that dengue vaccine should not be administered to children traveling to or visiting endemic dengue areas.
recommendations for infants born to mothers who have received positive test results for hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg)
meningococcal serogroups A, C, W, Y vaccine (MenACWY), meningococcal serogroup B vaccine (MenB)
describe the use of IPV in persons aged 18 years who are at increased risk for exposure to polioviruses.
inactivated poliovirus vaccine (IPV), and varicella vaccine.
approved the Recommended Child and Adolescent Immunization Schedule for Ages 18 Years or Younger, United States, 2023.
